transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My mind feels foggy all the time now, and I just can’t focus or make simple decisions at work. It’s like my brain is stuck in molasses, and even trying to figure out where to hang a shirt feels completely overwhelming.
Have you experienced these periods of feeling 'foggy' and overwhelmed before in your life, or is this the first time you have ever felt this way?

No, this is the first time I’ve ever felt like this. I used to really thrive at my job and love my hobbies, but this foggy, overwhelmed state started about two months ago after a corporate restructuring and missing out on a promotion.
Since this started after the restructuring, have you noticed if your mood or ability to function significantly improves when you are away from work or in situations unrelated to that event?

No, it doesn't get any better when I'm away from work. Even on my days off, I just lie on the couch staring at the wall and cancel on my friends because I feel so drained and hopeless. I can't even get myself to do basic chores around the house anymore.
Beyond feeling drained and overwhelmed, have you been experiencing other symptoms like a loss of appetite, changes in your sleep patterns, or persistent feelings of worthlessness?

Yes, to all of those. I have barely any appetite and my work pants are getting loose, and I keep waking up around 3 or 4 AM with my heart racing, unable to fall back asleep. I just feel like a complete failure who has let everyone down, and I feel like the drop in sales at work is entirely my fault.

Have you noticed any moments where your thoughts become so disorganized that you have trouble distinguishing reality from your own fears, or have you ever felt like you are losing touch with the world around you?

It’s hard to talk about, but I’ve been terrified lately that the store cameras and even my phone are being used by corporate to watch me specifically because they know I'm failing. My manager says it's just standard security, but I can't stop believing they are out to get me. On the rare days when I feel a tiny bit better, I can see how extreme that sounds, but most of the time it feels completely real.
When you have these thoughts about being watched, do you also hear voices talking to you, or see things that other people say are not there?

No, I don't hear any voices or see things that aren't there. It's strictly just this strong, constant conviction that they are watching me through the store cameras and my phone. I don't actually see or hear anything unusual, I'm just completely convinced it's happening.

The emergence of mood-congruent delusions (persecutory beliefs related to work failure) without hallucinations specifically points to a depressive episode with psychotic symptoms. F32.2 is excluded as it does not account for the presence of these delusions.
